_what: The instance half of the phone control panel (arsenal/panel/): WHICH services may be started and stopped from the phone, HOW each one is started, stopped and measured, and the video feed's addresses. Code reads this file; it never carries these facts itself.
_readme: Every value here is the HOUSE default a fork inherits. This machine's own values -- where OpenRGB is installed, which seat the link card reports -- live in the private profile (akashic-local/profile/phone-panel.json) and are laid over this file by core.local.load() before arsenal/panel/spec.py validates it. See docs/PHONE-PANEL.md for the drill that exercises this file.
_two_planes: REPO-VALUE here, MACHINE-VALUE in the private profile. A path written as ${INSTANCE_ROOT}/... or a leading ~ is a DERIVATION and belongs here; an absolute path that names this machine's disk does not (Rill's A1, 2026-10-31). A key that is `null` is a machine value the profile must supply -- the public file refuses to guess it, and the panel reports the row honestly instead of starting something in the wrong directory.
_rule: No entry here may name a command STRING. `start` is a LIST of arguments; `stop` is one of task_end / service_stop / kill_argv / none. A request from the phone can name only a service id and a verb -- it cannot reach any argument in this file, which is why none of these are injection surface.

panel._what: What the screen says about the seat it is reporting on. `agent: null` means: ask the private profile, then $AKASHIC_AGENT_ID, then report an empty seat rather than a guessed one.

services.label: Discord gateway

stop.why: the gateway is NEVER hand-killed. The house's revive ladder is the only lever: it observes, skips a healthy gateway and heals a dead one. A stop button here would be a hand-kill wearing a nicer label.

services._why: start and restart both call the revive ladder, which is a RECONCILER: on an already-healthy gateway it changes nothing. That is the intended shape -- Daniel's phone can ask 'make it reachable', not 'kill it'.

services.label: VJ engine
services._why: With FL Studio open the engine runs in GUEST mode by itself, so no flag is needed for either case.

services.label: Stage preview 8796
services._why: Measured 2026-10-31: the preview runs from a stage worktree of this checkout, which is what the ${INSTANCE_ROOT} derivation says. A machine that serves it from somewhere else overrides `start_cwd` in its own profile.

services.label: Stage preview 8798
services._why: Also the port the PhoneLink watcher already forwards to the phone, so the preview is one tap from this panel.

services.label: Bus runner (deepseek)

stop.why: a runner is a CHILD of its daemon, held by the runner lock (RB-21). The house moves a runner by reviving the daemon, not by killing the child: a hand-killed runner leaves the lock and the daemon's supervision disagreeing about who owns the seat.

services._why: `--target daemon` is a reconciler: it skips the daemons already healthy and raises only the dead, so this button is safe to press on a healthy fleet.

services.label: Bus runner (kimi)

stop.why: same rule as the deepseek runner: the daemon and the runner lock own this seat, so the revive ladder is the lever and a hand-kill is not.

services._why: The revive ladder also picks the right runner SCRIPT per agent (a resurrected daemon that omitted --runner-script would spawn the wrong seat's runner). That is exactly the bug this row refuses to reintroduce from a phone.

services.label: Play tracker
services._why: The tracker runs as a scheduled task whose script lives OUTSIDE this repo; that path is a machine value and sits in the private profile's playlog tenant, never here. Restart = end then run, which is the documented restart from the 2026-10-30 SMTC work. Its state is read with `schtasks /query`; if that cannot be read the row says UNKNOWN, not DOWN.

services.label: OpenRGB server
services._why: START IS NOT DECLARED HERE ON PURPOSE. OpenRGB is an external tool at an absolute path that belongs to this machine, so its argv and working directory live in the private profile (akashic-local/profile/phone-panel.json). Without that overlay the row is probe+stop: the panel can still tell Daniel whether the SDK server is up, and it refuses to start a tool it cannot locate rather than spawning a guess. Measured 2026-10-31: the desk themes and the RGB bridge both talk to 127.0.0.1:6742, so this row's state is also their precondition.

services.label: Memory watch
services._why: A sampler: it writes a durable JSONL. Killing it loses nothing but the samples it has not taken.

services.label: Apollo (video host)

probe.why: Apollo is not installed on this PC (2026-10-31: no Windows service matching Apollo, no Apollo directory under Program Files). The video card shows this state until it is installed.

services._why: No start and no stop are declared, so this row renders with NO buttons and a red dot that means 'the video feed does not exist yet', not 'it broke'. When Apollo is installed, this row gains a service probe and an argv -- and nothing else in the panel changes.

services.label: Rill's own DSH process
services.why_no_actions: the house rule: nobody touches Rill's own DSH process from another surface. Watched here because its state is the answer to 'is the seat that built this page alive'.

services.label: Claude wake listener
services.why_no_actions: a phone-triggered listener would be untracked by the harness: it would wake turns nobody armed and no ledger entry would explain it.

services.label: PhoneLink watcher
services.why_no_actions: restarting it from the phone cuts the phone off, because the watcher IS the tunnel this page arrives through. Restart it at the PC keyboard, never from here.

video._what: The two ends of the video feed, as DECLARED values. Daniel's ruling: video = Apollo + Artemis (Serge suggests Artemis instead of moonlight; Artemis's full features need Apollo, the same author's Sunshine fork).

apollo_web.why: Apollo's web UI has no address here because Apollo is not installed. Fill this in when it is, and this line becomes the card's second button.

artemis.label: Artemis
artemis.why: DECLARED, NOT VERIFIED: the package name com.limelight.artemis has not been checked against Daniel's install (the phone was unreachable while this was built). If the button answers 'no app can open this', correct THIS LINE -- that is one edit, and the failure is visible rather than silent.
